verdict: Purchases spiked this period, but the signal needs time to confirm.
narrative: Over the last 28 days, your Meta ads returned $3.54 for every $1.00 spent on $1,500.31 in total spend — a strong headline number, though the purchase volume is clustered on a handful of days rather than spread evenly across the period. The week-over-week jump in purchases and return on ad spend is real, but three of those days (Aug 15–17) produced only 3 purchases between them, so we're treating this as a promising signal rather than a confirmed trend reversal. Separately, Google Business Profile engagement dropped sharply in the last week, with local actions falling to zero over Aug 15–17 after averaging roughly 17 per day through July — we're actively monitoring this to ensure your local visibility doesn't slip while paid performs. The live-cooking content shoot, originally scheduled for Aug 14, is being rescheduled so fresh creative can enter the ad pipeline; new real-footage ads are expected to reduce audience fatigue and support reach, which has compressed roughly 33% over the past four weeks. By end of August, the funnel test closes and UTM tracking goes live, which will give us a cleaner read on exactly where purchases are coming from going forward.
